=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly arise from the same node in a circular arrangement)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are gathered closely at the terminal end of the visible stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf blade is undivided and attached directly to the stem)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth and continuous, though some leaves show damage with missing sections)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate (leaf is broadest near the tip and tapers towards the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tip comes to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (leaf tapers gradually to a wedge-like base where it attaches to the petiole)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with veins branching off to the sides)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, spaced widely, curving towards the leaf margin
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous, dull (surface appears smooth without hairs and has a non-glossy finish)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are very short and barely visible where the leaf meets the stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (appears cylindrical, though details are obscured by the close attachment)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the stem appears rigid and brownish, typical of a young tree seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent
    19. Stem color: brown
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no clear stipules are visible at the leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a distinct whorled arrangement of leaves. Several leaves show physical damage in the form of holes and missing margins. The leaves are uniformly green with a dull finish.
